title: SR-1.29 A hook starts without loading the whole CLI
request: Closes G94: the MEM-098 latency test (test/hooks-latency.test.mjs:64: the prompt hook returns in under 1.5 s while each backend call takes 1 s) fails on the CI runner at 1589 to 1729 ms on 32 of 37 open pull requests, after passing on 28 to 30 October. The hook runs through bin/memev.mjs, which loads the whole CLI (src/cli/main.mjs) for every hook, and src/cli/hooks.mjs loads the engine at start through isVault (src/engine/vault.mjs) and the transcript scanner. Measured on 31 October 2026 on a development machine: node starts in 40 ms, importing main.mjs takes 110 ms and hooks.mjs 140 ms, and the test passes there at 1322 ms. Every hook event calls isVault, which lives in the engine module (src/engine/vault.mjs:39). The fix is to the hook's own start-up, never to the budget. Repository: memev. Depends on contracts: QL-1.02. Its design landed on main first as a stopgap (pull request 267, squash 2bfaa7d936c192cc24bebf1adf6575253f32ba44). The contract's explicit base is 8b377f107e4c0c601420c7f3182be3d9e366a2bf, the commit before that squash, and the work is verified on a branch that starts at the squash with no merge of main before verify, so the red runs and every base comparison see the code before the stopgap and the range holds only this contract's commits.

tasks.title: The hook path starts light
requirements: bin/memev.mjs hands a hook command (memev hook <event>) to src/cli/hooks.mjs before it imports src/cli/main.mjs; every other command path is unchanged

src/cli/hooks.mjs imports at module load only what every hook event needs; the engine (src/engine/vault.mjs and what it imports), the transcript scanner and any code one event alone uses are imported inside that event's path

isVault and STATE move to a new module, src/engine/vault-marker.mjs, that imports only node built-ins, and src/engine/vault.mjs re-exports both, so there is one definition of 'is a vault' and a hook checks it without loading the engine
the hooks' behaviour, output and exit codes are unchanged, and the 1.5 s budget of MEM-098, MEMEV_HOOK_BUDGET_MS and test/hooks-latency.test.mjs stay as they are
the start-up cost is measured, not assumed: the test records which modules a hook process loads and how long a prompt hook takes with a stub that answers at once

a hook process reaches the daemon on this computer with node:http directly (useDirectLoopback in src/cli/common.mjs, called only by bin/memev.mjs on the hook path); every other caller keeps fetchOut, which src/cli/common.mjs imports only when first used

bin/memev.mjs takes the hook path only when the first argument is exactly hook; every other command, memev contract hook included, goes through main() with its error output (memev: <message> on stderr, the stack under MEMEV_DEBUG) and exit codes unchanged
every dynamic import on the hook path is a string-literal relative specifier, so it resolves on Windows and never from the app's working directory
the production entry points never enable a code cache or register module hooks; the load log is a test helper only
the MEM-098 tests pass on a loaded machine: ten runs in a row with one busy process per CPU

criteria.statement: Spawned as node bin/memev.mjs hook <event> --client claude-code against a stub daemon, with a module-load log (a resolve hook registered through --import from test/helpers/load-log.mjs): the prompt event loads none of src/cli/main.mjs, src/engine/vault.mjs and src/cli/transcript.mjs, and no hook event loads src/cli/main.mjs.
